target_customer: Peruvian middle class consumers who pay interest on small instant loans and point of sale financing
problem: Many Peruvians lack credit cards, so they cannot finance small purchases or emergencies. Apurata offers instant underwriting for purchases of 100 to 1000 dollars.
business_model: Consumer lending with interest and fees, point of sale financing through retailers (aCuotaz) and microloans
product_category: Consumer credit and point of sale financing

founders.name: José E. Carrillo Pino
founders.background_notes: YC page: experienced software developer, first startup, started right after university (university not named).

founders.name: Patrick Wakeham
prior_employers: DB (investment banking, 7 years, as written on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says self taught programmer.

technical_complexity.rationale: Instant credit scoring with limited data in Peru plus payments and collections integrations is standard fintech engineering with some hard modeling.

defensibility.rationale: A SBS licence as a Casa de Prestamos (resolution 04852-2019) and repayment data helped, but capital was the real constraint.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy was found. The company continues operating in Peru only.

market_need_then: Credit card penetration in Peru was low, so point of sale credit for small purchases had demand. The company claimed over 56 thousand loans delivered and 97 million soles financed in a later interview (date not shown).

identity.logo: Wordmark with tagline Mejores Prestamos on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain Spanish, instant loans with minimal paperwork

branding.community_and_virality: Company site lists coverage by Peruvian outlets (El Comercio, La Republica, Peru21, Gestion, Andina) and social accounts for Apurata and aCuotaz.

brand_strength.rationale: Local press coverage listed by the company itself and a secondary product brand (aCuotaz), but no independent evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Apurata is active with about 12 people in Peru and still offers small digital loans of 100 to 1000 soles. Verified funding is limited to the YC investment and aggregator figures near 200 thousand dollars, so growth appears modest and the lender may be constrained by funding for its loan book. It holds a SBS licence from 2019. Whether it scales beyond Peru is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: Caplight lists 210,000 dollars total with last round 2019-08-19 (investors Y Combinator, 500 Global, Start-Up Peru) and CB Insights lists 220K. These are aggregators only, so no rounds are recorded. The company site links to 500 Startups Latin America batch eight. In the Infomercado interview, Wakeham said YC invested about 150,000 dollars on average and that the company was before a Series A. Competitors Addi, Aplazo and Kueski come from a CB Insights comparison with no 2019 date (Aplazo was founded 2020), so none are listed. Founding year conflicts (2016 on CB Insights, 2017 on YC). No outcome news found.
